question: Can the validated behavioral+structural parallel-channel freshness-detection architecture (orthogonality confirmed at delta=0.15 across 6 independent localhost mock experiments, r=0.002-0.046, CI upper 0.06-0.135, all TOST PASS, audit PASS) be wired into the SPIDER kernel (src/spider/kernel.py) as a freshness-check subprocess that runs without new LLM calls, using HTTP requests to the mechanism's target endpoint to detect auth/session/API drift — and does the integration (a) correctly gate resolution of stale mechanisms, (b) preserve the orthogonality property at delta=0.15, (c) add less than 200ms latency overhead per resolution call, and (d) not regress the existing kernel test suite?
hypothesis: A freshness_check() subprocess added to SpiderKernel that probes the mechanism's endpoint via HTTP and computes a behavioral_score (token/session/auth drift detection) and a structural_score (ETag/Cache-Control/response-hash drift detection) will: (1) detect expired/invalid tokens with TP >= 0.85 when the mechanism's auth_scope is stale; (2) tolerate structural noise (optional field churn, response-time jitter, field-type normalization) with FP <= 0.10; (3) maintain behavioral-structural orthogonality at delta=0.15 (stratified pooled Pearson r CI upper < 0.15, TOST p_upper < 0.05); (4) gate resolution by returning ResolutionStatus.STALE for mechanisms whose behavioral freshness_score exceeds a calibrated threshold, causing resolve() to return UNKNOWN for stale mechanisms; (5) add < 200ms median latency overhead per resolve() call on localhost; (6) pass all existing kernel tests without modification.
falsifier: The integration is FALSIFIED if ANY of: (F1) behavioral drift detection TP < 0.85 on expired-token drift across 3 endpoints (the parallel-channel architecture's validated detection capability is lost during kernel wiring); (F2) structural noise FP > 0.10 on 240 noise-only samples (the architecture's noise tolerance is lost); (F3) behavioral-structural orthogonality breaks: stratified pooled Pearson r CI upper >= 0.15 OR TOST p_upper >= 0.05 at delta=0.15 (the independence property that justifies the parallel-channel architecture is destroyed by kernel integration); (F4) any existing kernel test in tests/test_kernel.py fails after integration (the integration introduces a regression); (F5) median latency overhead >= 200ms per resolve() call (the subprocess is too expensive for production use).

baselines.description: Current kernel.py resolve() with no freshness checking — the default baseline representing the status quo. Mechanisms are resolved purely by intent match, preconditions, applicability guards, parameter_slots, and confidence. No HTTP probes, no drift detection.
baselines.expected: resolve() returns EXECUTABLE for any mechanism whose preconditions match, regardless of staleness. All existing tests pass. Zero latency overhead from freshness.

baselines.description: Freshness gate using only behavioral_score (token validation failure rate, session state change). Structural signals are not computed. This tests whether behavioral alone is sufficient for kernel gating.
baselines.expected: TP >= 0.85 on expired tokens, but may have higher FP on structural noise if behavioral signal alone cannot distinguish drift from noise. Orthogonality not applicable (single channel).

baselines.description: Freshness gate using only structural_score (ETag/Cache-Control header cardinality, response-body hash). Behavioral signals are not computed. This tests whether structural alone is sufficient.
baselines.expected: FP <= 0.10 on structural noise (structural channel is noise-tolerant per validated architecture), but TP may be < 0.85 on expired tokens (structural channel does not detect auth drift per validated architecture).

positive_control.description: Mechanism with auth_scope='bearer' stored against a Flask+PyJWT mock endpoint. Token is expired (JWT exp claim in the past). The freshness_check() probe sends an HTTP request with the expired token and receives 401. Behavioral signal should detect the drift (behavioral_score > threshold). Structural signal should be independent (ETag/Cache-Control still present on 401 response body). TP >= 0.85 required.
positive_control.implementation: Reuse the existing EXP-PRODUCT-35445596342 testbed_server.py mock (Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256 + SQLite WAL + TTL cache). Mechanism stored with auth_scope matching the mock's JWT configuration. Probe target: /api/user/profile endpoint.

null_control.description: Mechanism with valid (non-expired) token. Structural noise patterns applied: optional_field_addition (add 1-5 unused fields to /api/schema response), description_change (modify descriptive text), response_time_jitter (add 10-100ms uniform delay), field_type_normalization (change field types in schema). FP <= 0.10 required — behavioral signal must not fire on structural noise.
null_control.implementation: Same testbed_server.py mock with noise injection via query parameters (?noise=optional_field_addition&size=10). 240 noise-only samples (4 noise types x 60 each).

measurement_validity: 1. The freshness_check() subprocess must use real HTTP requests to the mock endpoint (not mocked/deterministic responses) — this tests the actual kernel→HTTP→signal pipeline.
2. Behavioral and structural signals must be computed from HTTP response attributes (headers, status code, body), not from internal kernel state or mechanism metadata.
3. The orthogonality measurement must use endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r on non-304 samples only, matching the validated protocol from EXP-GRAPH-35353011131 and EXP-PRODUCT-35445596342.
4. Latency measurement must use time.perf_counter() around the freshness_check() call only (not including mock server startup), averaged over 100 resolve() calls.
5. The existing kernel tests must be run unmodified (tests/test_kernel.py) to verify no regression.
6. The freshness gate must NOT use LLM calls — the subprocess must be purely HTTP-based signal computation. This is a hard constraint from the Director mandate.

7. The structural signal must use headers-only extraction (ETag, Cache-Control, request_id entropy) matching the validated protocol. Body-hash structural signal is excluded due to the V1 confound identified in EXP-GRAPH-35445595108.
8. Token management for the mock must use a single JWT signing key (HS256 shared secret) to avoid the RSA key-sharing confound from EXP-GRAPH-35572179326.
decision_rule: The kernel integration SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST if ALL of: (C1) behavioral drift detection TP >= 0.85 across all 3 endpoints on expired-token positive control (PC-EXPIRED-TOKEN); (C2) behavioral FP rate <= 0.10 on 240 noise-only samples (NC-STRUCTURAL-NOISE); (C3) at least 2/3 endpoints have behavioral_signal_std > 0.05 AND at least 2/3 have structural_signal_std > 0.05 in the 8 co-occurring conditions; (C4) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 samples only) < 0.15 AND TOST p_upper < 0.05 at delta=0.15; (C5) all 3 existing kernel tests in tests/test_kernel.py pass without modification; (C6) median latency overhead per freshness_check() call < 200ms (measured over 100 calls on localhost). The integration is FALSIFIED if ANY condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if the mock endpoint is unreachable or the testbed construction fails.
product_consequence_positive: C-FRESHNESS advances from EXPERIMENTAL toward PRODUCT_CORE. The kernel gains end-to-end freshness detection without LLM calls. Parallel-channel architecture is justified for integration into the shipping kernel at the localhost mock ceiling. Product can proceed to: (a) n>=800 non-304 re-run for delta=0.10 inference; (b) distributed CDN/OAuth validation; (c) broader task corpus integration.
product_consequence_negative: C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL. The validated parallel-channel architecture cannot be wired into the kernel without losing its detection/orthogonality properties. Product must either: (a) redesign the freshness gate with a different signal extraction approach; (b) accept that freshness detection requires a standalone subprocess outside the kernel; (c) pivot to alternative freshness mechanisms (e.g., periodic background re-validation).
estimated_cost: Low: single GitHub Actions run, ~500 HTTP requests to localhost mock, zero LLM calls, zero external API calls. Estimated wall-clock: < 5 minutes. Infrastructure: Python 3.12, Flask 3.1.3, PyJWT 2.14.0, requests 2.34.2 (all already installed per parent audit).
expected_information_gain: High: this is the minimum-cost experiment that resolves the single binding question from the Director mandate — whether the validated C-FRESHNESS architecture can be productized into the kernel. A positive result (SURVIVES) changes a product architecture decision (parallel-channel justified for kernel integration). A negative result (FALSIFIED) identifies the specific integration failure mode and redirects product strategy. Either outcome is decisive for C-FRESHNESS claim advancement.
